title: State and Configuration
objective: Understand how STATE.md and config.json track project state and settings across sessions

content.value:
GSD needs to remember things between sessions: which phase you are on, what decisions were made, how the project is configured. Two files handle this:

  .planning/config.json — Project settings (model profile, granularity, feature flags)
  .planning/STATE.md    — Current position, decisions, blockers, session continuity

config.json is a simple JSON file with flat key-value pairs. GSD reads it with loadConfig(), which always returns a valid object — if the file is missing or corrupted, it falls back to sensible defaults. This defensive pattern appears throughout GSD.

The try/catch with silent fallback is GSD's standard pattern for loading persisted state. You will see it in loadProgress() (the progress tracker), loadConfig(), and state parsing. The principle: never crash on bad data, always have a safe default.

STATE.md is a Markdown file parsed with regular expressions — no YAML frontmatter, no Markdown parser dependency. GSD reads it as a string and uses regex to find sections. This is intentional: STATE.md is human-readable and human-editable, while still machine-parseable.

This completes the command lifecycle. You have traced a GSD command from user input (gsd-tools.cjs) through dispatch (switch statement) to handler functions (lib/*.cjs) that read and write state (config.json, STATE.md). Every GSD command follows this exact path.

successCriteria: You can explain the loadConfig defensive pattern and how STATE.md is parsed with regex instead of a Markdown library
